title: Workspaces can be put in named groups in the sidebar
body:
The sidebar shows every workspace in one list. `Frame::new` in `src/server/chrome/frame.rs` sorts the entries by their most urgent agent state, attention first, and keeps the picker's order within a state. The open sidebar draws a card per entry (`Frame::cards`), and the closed sidebar draws a tile per entry (`Frame::tiles`). Jack keeps work and personal workspaces, and does not want their cards mixed and sorted together.

## Proposal

A group is a named set of workspaces. It means nothing to decade outside the sidebar.

- Ungrouped workspaces stay at the top of the sidebar and sort as they do now.
- Each group follows them under a header with its name, and sorts its own cards the same way.
- Right-clicking dead space in the open sidebar offers "new group", from the context menu in decade-98702c.
- Jack drags a card onto a group to move it there, and drags it to the ungrouped area to take it out. The context menu offers both moves too.
- Deleting a group returns its workspaces to ungrouped.
- A group is renamed the same way as a workspace (decade-e8cf5c).
- Super+A still jumps to the next workspace in attention across all groups, and the top bar's state counts stay totals.

## Cost

Groups and their members are saved with the workspaces in `src/server/save.rs`. The save format's `VERSION` moves from 2 to 3, and the reader keeps an arm for version 2.

## Open

- How the closed sidebar's tiles show where one group ends and the next begins, such as a gap or a thin rule, so the order does not change unexplained when the sidebar closes.
- Whether a group folds to its header. A folded group with an agent in attention would need to say so on the header.
- Where a new group goes among the existing groups, and whether Jack can reorder groups by dragging their headers.
